title: REPORT on public procurement
part_text: 18. Notes that, at present, public contracting authorities already have the option to consider factors such as innovation, resilience, sustainability and social considerations via award, technical specification or contract performance clauses, merely on a voluntary basis and depending on their decision, as explicitly permitted by the 2014 directives; notes that in certain cases public contracts continue to be awarded primarily on the basis of a lowest price criterion, also owing to insufficient training and financial and human resources, restricting procurement authorities from considering additional factors such as innovation and quality-to-price ratio, which leads to suboptimal long-term outcomes that are misaligned with citizens’ interests; stresses that reliance on the lowest-price criterion limits the ability of contracting authorities to take into account operational costs and to apply life cycle costing;
